A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowBind work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, ablations, latent-space analyses, robustness examples, and experiments extending FlowBind to 3D point clouds.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative experiments, including the results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices E–H.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same shared latent, modality-specific invertible flows, training objective and gradient strategy, and inference through backward flows, latent averaging, and forward flows. The architectures and 3D extension also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same text, image, and audio datasets and generation scenarios, including MS-COCO evaluation and synthetic AudioCaps triplets. The Pix3D point-cloud extension and unseen cross-modal combinations already appear in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–6 and Appendix H are unchanged, including CoDi, OmniFlow, UnifiedIO2-L, the specialist models, and the text-anchoring control in their respective comparisons. BBDM and SemFlow are new citations, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the same held-out and zero-shot evaluations, synthetic-triplet construction, metrics, training budgets, and analysis procedures. Settings such as 200K training iterations, batch size 1024, and the CKNNA sample and neighborhood sizes are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendices E–H retain the same anchor ablation, CKNNA analysis, latent interpolation and clustering, conflicting-condition robustness test, unseen point-cloud combinations, and qualitative cases. No analysis or supporting example is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and rankings in the corresponding tables, along with the qualitative examples and findings, are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains FlowBind's text-to-image FID of 17.39 and audio-to-text CIDEr of 55.11.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, Proposition 1's conditional-variance decomposition, and Appendix A's assumptions and complete proof remain unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, or formal claim is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient any-to-any generation from arbitrarily paired data, jointly learned shared latent and flows, and competitive quality with reduced data and computation. Copyediting does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of image–audio performance, data efficiency, balanced conditioning, latent-space semantics, and robustness remain the same. Neither version adds or removes a substantive limitation, failure condition, or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same algorithms, encoder/decoder choices, 768-dimensional features, training recipe, hardware, and reported training time. The project-page URL and code/data-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 broadens its description of direct mappings from two modalities to two data distributions and adds BBDM (Li et al., 2023) and SemFlow (Wang et al., 2024a). The existing text–image references and FlowBind's principal positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammatical and typographical corrections, modestly revises the related-work paragraph, and expands the acknowledgments. The running header changes from Preprint to an ICLR 2026 publication notice; section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 receive revised header typography, spacing, and separator rules, including clearer separation of the FlowBind row. Updated running headers and local text/reference reflow are limited layout changes; figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The BBDM and SemFlow citations make Section 4's coverage of prior data-to-data models more complete, while grammatical corrections and table formatting modestly improve readability. The scientific evidence, theory, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
